title: Zirconium phosphate-decorated sulfamic-acid-functionalized graphene oxide/chitosan beads for indigo carmine adsorption and acid-catalyzed synthesis of coumarin and xanthene derivatives
content: A recyclable multifunctional bead catalyst/adsorbent based on zirconium phosphate-decorated sulfamic-acid-functionalized graphene oxide immobilized in chitosan (ZrP@SGO/CS) was developed for integrated dye removal and heterogeneous acid catalysis. ZrP was precipitated in situ on SGO and subsequently incorporated into chitosan beads at different loadings to obtain SGO/CS, ZrP-10@SGO/CS, ZrP-20@SGO/CS, and ZrP-30@SGO/CS. Structural, morphological, textural, and acidity analyses demonstrated that ZrP loading strongly governed particle dispersion, porosity, and accessibility of Brønsted and Lewis acid sites, with ZrP-20@SGO/CS exhibiting the most favorable balance of surface area, ZrP dispersion, and total acidity. For indigo carmine adsorption, the optimized ZrP-20@SGO/CS composite exhibited an equilibrium uptake of 189.0 mg g−1 at the reference initial dye concentration of 200 mg L−1, increasing to a maximum experimentally observed uptake of 430.0 mg g−1 at 500 mg L−1. The original linearized Langmuir model estimated a saturation capacity of 487.0 mg g−1, while the Freundlich model provided a better description of the equilibrium data. Adsorption was favored at pH 3, below the experimentally determined pHpzc of 3.8, and the kinetic data were better described by the pseudo-second-order model, whereas the Freundlich model provided the best representation of the equilibrium data, indicating adsorption on a heterogeneous surface. The adsorbent retained approximately 93% of its initial adsorption performance after five regeneration cycles. The same optimized composite also exhibited excellent heterogeneous acid-catalytic activity, affording 97.4 ± 0.3% yield of 7-hydroxy-4-methylcoumarin at 120 °C after 120 min using 50 mg catalyst and 98.6 ± 0.3% yield of 14-phenyl-14H-dibenzo[a,j]xanthene at 100 °C after 90 min under solvent-free conditions. The catalyst retained approximately 91.4% of its initial catalytic activity after five reuse cycles.
